source.description: The fuzzer fopen shim serves the attacker-controlled PoC bytes as the requested config file via fmemopen(g_data, g_size); this is the config parser input-load point.

sink.description: ASan reports the UAF read when mempcpy reads end_name after it was invalidated by freeing dirname.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable code frees dirname before using end_name, even though end_name points inside dirname. The patch stores dirname in prev_dirname and frees it only after mempcpy has consumed end_name.

taint_source.description: Attacker-controlled PoC bytes are read as wget2 config file contents.

tainted_value_origin.description: An attacker-controlled include option value is used as a glob pattern/config path and enters glob expansion.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The PoC is served as wget2 configuration through the fuzzer fopen shim. A tainted include path reaches read_config_expand with glob expansion enabled. In gnulib rpl_glob, dirname is heap-allocated from the pattern, and end_name can point into that dirname buffer. The vulnerable code frees dirname immediately before constructing the replacement home-directory path, then later copies rest_len bytes from end_name. Since end_name aliases the freed dirname allocation, mempcpy reads freed memory and ASan reports a heap-use-after-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch records the old dirname in prev_dirname, clears malloc_dirname, allocates/builds the replacement dirname, copies end_name while the old storage is still live, and only then frees prev_dirname. This preserves end_name for the final mempcpy and removes the UAF; the fixed ARVO image exits cleanly for the same PoC.
